newsitem.title: CHINA: Warnings shadow North Korean defector's birthday.
newsitem.headline: Warnings shadow North Korean defector's birthday.

text.p: The most senior leader ever to defect from North Korea passed his 74th birthday quietly behind a police cordon in Beijing on Monday as former comrades outside demanded his return and issued harsh warnings to rival Seoul.

Hwang Jang-yop, a top adviser to North Korea's supreme leader Kim Jong-il, spent his sixth day as the focus of an international diplomatic crisis centred on the South Korean mission in Beijing, where he sought refuge on Wednesday.

North Korean officials keeping vigil outside the Chinese police cordon around the mission accused South Korea of kidnapping Hwang and issued dour warnings of the consequences of any attempt to move him out of Beijing to the South.
"If they make him go to Seoul, I think there will be war," said one official who declined to be identified.
"We want him back," he said, in an echo of earlier threats to use force if Hwang was compelled to go to Seoul.
China, an unwilling third party in the feuding between the two hostile ends of the Korean peninsula, has appealed to both sides to act calmly to resolve the affair.
South Korean diplomats in Beijing said they had no plans to brief reporters over the next few days, suggesting they did not expect the diplomatic crisis to end soon.

The United States has urged Pyongyang to avoid all provocative actions and has said it is closely monitoring developments after an assassination attempt against a former North Korean defector near Seoul on Saturday night.

South Korea accused Pyongyang agents of shooting 32-year-old defector Li Il-nam in an attack that left him critically ill with a bullet still lodged in his skull. Doctors in Seoul said he was on life support and was unlikely to regain consciousness.

Analysts say the North has suffered huge loss of face over the defection of Hwang, who was ranked high in the hierarchy of his Stalinist homeland and was the architect of its governing ideology of Juche, or strict self-reliance.

The most senior defection from North Korea comes as the communist hermit nation struggles to cope with an imploding economy and widespread food shortages caused by two years of flood disasters and failed harvests.

Analysts found little trace of true festivity in Pyongyang's celebrations to mark Kim Jong-il's 55th birthday on Sunday, but North Korean officials in Beijing rushed to ram home the message that the son of former President Kim Il-sung was in command.
"Comrade Kim Jong-il is the father of his people, a man of lofty humanity," said a report issued by Pyongyang diplomats.
"The leader Kim Jong-il has never met with a single political failure for more than three decades," it said.
The tussle over Hwang's defection is the latest flare-up in ever-tense relations between the two Koreas, arch-enemies since the 1950-53 Korean civil war ended only in a truce.
South Korean officials have said the scholarly theoretician is spending his time reading and sleeping at the mission but have given no details on how he would mark his birthday.

Chinese paramilitary and regular police have steadily stepped up their guard around the mission, stationing a crowd control truck armed with water cannon and a bullet-proof car outside and flooding the area with armed officers at night.

Officers laid bands of anti-tyre spikes across the pavement of the quiet tree-lined streets of the diplomatic quarter and turned away scores of would-be Chinese travellers seeking visas at the South Korean consular offices in the mission.

"It took two days on the train to get here...but the office is closed," said one ethnic-Korean visa-seeker from the northeastern Chinese province of Heilongjiang who had hoped to complete the formalities needed to marry a South Korean man.
"We don't know when the office will open again, they haven't told us anything," she said.
